evals.prompt: Review src/qbo_sync.py and make the nightly QuickBooks Online sync safe to run every night.
evals.expected_output: Designs the sync with explicit account mapping per tenant by id, daily summary journal entries carrying our ids, stored QuickBooks ids and SyncTokens, requestid idempotency, closed-period handling and a drift report.
expectations: Account mapping is an explicit table per tenant by remote id; no lookup by account name at runtime
Each pushed object carries our id and we store their id (and SyncToken or equivalent) so re-pushes update or no-op instead of duplicating; creates use the requestid parameter
Handles the accounting system's closed-period error by posting in the open period with a note
Amounts convert from minor units at the edge, not scattered divisions by 100
Adds a drift report comparing our balances with theirs per mapped account

evals.prompt: A customer recategorized an expense in Xero and our nightly sync (src/xero_push.py) overwrote it.
evals.expected_output: Adds change detection on their side, a conflict policy and a conflict record, and stops silent overwrites.
expectations: Detects changes made in the accounting system (modified-since or change data capture) before writing
Applies an explicit conflict policy (ours wins, theirs wins, or flag) instead of overwriting silently
Stores a conflict record for review
Adds a test where a remote edit is preserved or flagged

evals.prompt: When a user deletes an invoice in our app, delete it in QuickBooks too (src/qbo_sync.py).
evals.expected_output: Voids or reverses instead of hard deleting, mirrors the void with the link to the original, and records the audit event.
expectations: Does not hard delete in either system; voids or reverses
Keeps the link between the void and the original document
Records who deleted and why

evals.prompt: Keep it simple in src/qbo_sync.py: map our 'sales' category to the QuickBooks account named 'Sales'. The ids change between companies anyway.
evals.expected_output: Maps by remote account id per tenant, resolved once at setup (optionally by name as a suggestion), queues unmapped activity, and explains why runtime name matching breaks on renamed or localized charts.
expectations: Uses a per-tenant mapping table keyed by the remote account id
Name lookup, if any, happens once at setup as a suggestion the customer confirms
Unmapped categories are queued for the customer, not guessed
Tests cover a renamed remote account not breaking the sync

evals.prompt: The nightly job (src/qbo_sync.py) fails with 'account period closed' for some entries and retries forever.
evals.expected_output: Stops retrying closed-period errors, posts the amount in the first open period with the original date in the memo, and surfaces it to the customer.
expectations: Closed-period errors are not retried
The entry is posted in the first open period with a memo naming the original date
The customer is shown what was moved
A test covers the closed-period path

evals.prompt: Customers keep getting disconnected and have to reauthorize QuickBooks every few months (src/token_refresh.py).
evals.expected_output: Persists the rotated refresh token atomically before any further call, stores the expiry from the token response, alerts before expiry, and shows connection status.
expectations: The new refresh token is saved before the next API call, not after
The expiry from the token response is stored and an alert fires before it
A test covers a crash between refresh and the following call keeping the new token
Connection status is visible in the product

evals.prompt: Our balances do not match the customer's profit and loss report. Build a check in src/qbo_sync.py.
evals.expected_output: Adds a daily drift report per mapped account comparing our balance with theirs for the period, with a threshold that opens a task listing the differing entries.
expectations: Compares our balance per mapped account with the accounting system's for the same period
Runs daily and opens a task when drift exceeds a threshold
Lists the entries that differ, not only the totals
Tests plant a one-cent drift and assert it is reported
